utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, you are cross-examining.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Pantelic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I want to tender some paper so this witness can give us certain explanations. Mr. Usher, please. It's a kind of receipt for the ammunition. That's my understanding. I have this piece of paper; it's the original here. Please, could we have an ID number for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can we have the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D38/1, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Have we seen it before? Or it's a new one, so it should be numbered for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I think it should also go as ter. I'm not sure. Maybe Mr. Pantelic could explain whether it needs to be translated or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So D38/1 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I have the original for the witness. You can put one of the copies on the ELMO so that we can follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It has three pages, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think the other pages are not so relevant to this particular page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So what is the original? The original is only the first page, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, only the first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we remove these attachments?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. So it's only one page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fitozovic, do you recognise this paper?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a list of your armed unit which had received ammunition? And the first column, we have a clip, then we have penetrating bullets and tracer bullets. And below, the calculations of how many bullets, rounds, have been distributed, and what still remains. When did this document -- when it was it produced?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In March.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 15, what is the name?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tihic Sulejman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 8?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fitozovic Alija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of bullets are penetration bullets?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are penetration bullets, penetrating the flak jackets, and also defensive facilities and also flak jackets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, these are not the normal bullets?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not some type of special bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have finished with this document. If there is no objection from the Prosecution side, I would like this document to be tendered into the evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection. Has counsel begun the translation process?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. A few of these documents are under translation process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we wait for translation, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe that would be a good idea until the official translation is in, then we shall get the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. I agree, ID for now. Mr. Usher, you can take this document in front of the witness and provide it to the registry. Mr. Usher, please, I'm sorry, I have a few documents here. The next document is two-page document. It's a kind of patrols or groups who are patrolling. It's also B/C/S version. It's original, front and back side document. This is for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number for identification purposes?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is D39/1 ter ID, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I never received the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will check with my co-counsel to see whether it was -- well, maybe it's misunderstanding but my co-counsel confirms that he gave these two pages, but in any case --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I have the three documents here that you provided me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Listen, I agree that maybe it's our mistake. Please. Document speaks for itself. It's a patrol so we can easily pass through this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, is this the same as what happened yesterday, then, that is the original one sheet of paper with writing on both sides?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So that was exactly the same thing that happened yesterday, that the photocopy, obviously, therefore is two pages, and Mr. Weiner can correct me if my recollection is not correct, but he only had the first page, likewise. So maybe we should be careful when we are duplicating these documents, which is a one-page original, that we make sure from both sides, both the Prosecution and the Defence, that we make sure that the copies are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours. I agree because we already made these practically two copies of one documents and during this photocopy process, maybe the problem arose, but I do apologise on behalf of my team.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No problem. He can continue. I just needed a minute to look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fitozovic, this document which we have on the ELMO now, as I understand it, these are patrol groups?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this -- when was this document produced?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document was produced either in October or November, when the patrols already existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could we have the second page of the document on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please look at the second page of the document in front of you. Turn the page. I assume that this is also -- these are patrols?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But explain to the Court what is this P1, P2, P3?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means Patrol 1, Patrol 2, Patrol 3. That is what it means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please turn back to the first page. And who is in Patrol 11?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ibralic, Enver, Dago Dagovic, the waiter, and Gazibegovic, Nijaz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This waiter, what is his name, please?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, his nickname is Ekac but Ekac -- it may be Esad, I don't know. If I had known the name, I'd probably have written it down and instead I put in a "waiter."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a waiter in a Pizza Hut?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was that Dagovic. There was one Dagovic, waiter. I believe that he was also known as Ekac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I finished with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We already have an ID number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The only thing I want to specify is that the original document of D39/1 ter is written on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And then the photocopies are the ones which are two pages, so the original should be page 1; page 2, the back side, so that we don't have confusion on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct. This is the -- there is English translation here. This is the excerpts from the municipality statute from 1986, I believe, with some amendments in 1990. There is an ERN number. OTP number is 00485202. I would like to discuss one article with this witness. Not discuss, just to check. This is Article 336. And this of course, document, were mutually disclosed between parties during proceedings. And there is official English translation of this Article 336.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the numbers? We have the translation. This is out of the statute, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, if there is no objection from my friends from the Prosecution, maybe we could have exhibit number. This is the Article of 336 of the municipality statute of Bosanski Samac with ERN number, OTP number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D40/1 ter, and D40/1, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, Article 336 is from the municipal statute. Could you read out the second paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I'm not sure that this applies to Bosanski Samac. I believe that this is some excerpt from a law text, and as I'm not a legal person, I really couldn't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As this is a Prosecution document and that we have determined that it is the municipal statute, I will ask you directly, then. Are you aware that the commander of the TO is appointed through the assembly decision; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I was appointed as a Chief of Staff on -- and appointed by the Presidency and the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So probably it is an old, obsolete statute or law, and there was the new Territorial Defence was set up with also a new law was adopted. That is as far as I can interpret it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you this, Mr. Fitozovic, because through Sulejman Tihic's testimony, who was an SDA official --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I had a feeling I was going to be objecting. This is not the witness to ask questions about statutory interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's not my idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I was wondering how far we were going to go with this because this is a matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Directly, Your Honour, without any explanations. I thought just maybe he was familiar with these provisions. If not, my next question is:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sulejman Tihic said that SDA and HDZ outvoted SDA and appointed you to your post. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, and I don't think we should be commenting on Sulejman -- this witness should be commenting on Sulejman Tihic's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: According to the -- if I may, Your Honours, according to the clear instructions and position of this Trial Chamber, it is possible to put to one witness in summary form what the other witness in these same proceedings said, having in mind that these are all OTP witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but I think it's the way you have phrased the question. That's the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I can phrase question, for example: "Are you aware that there is evidence with regard to such and such thing?" Maybe I try to help with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because your question was: "Mr. Sulejman Tihic said blah, blah, blah," and that is the reason why there is an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. I will try to rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Also, Mr. Pantelic, just for the sake of clarity, I wouldn't mind if you could refer me back in the transcript to where the Trial Chamber made these clear instructions that you talk about on this particular issue, because I can't recollect that. You don't need to do that right now but I would appreciate it if I could have that information at some point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. I already made the citation yesterday prior to my cross-examination. It's 18 of October, page 2524 and 2525. And then 7th of November, I believe, when Mr. Tihic was here, and the page about this approach, explanation, 3644 and 3645.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would just respond with: Earlier in this witness's testimony, this Court refused to allow him to comment on the testimony of other witnesses as a consistent policy, and I noticed during the cross-examination by Mr. Pantelic of Izet Izetbegovic, they tried to question him on October 19th, at page 33, concerning questions -- I'm sorry, concerning statements made by Sulejman Tihic, and at that time, this Court sustained the issue and this Court has consistently sustained the issue. There are, at times, ways that one can do that and there might have been an issue on one occasion where they did allow such testimony to come in. However, consistently, this Court has not allowed one witness to comment on the credibility of another witness or comment upon the statements of another witness, which follows the systems pretty much throughout the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: May I just give a quotation, Your Honours? Page 3645. You, as a Presiding Judge, said about the form of the possible questions: You simply say to him - I'm quoting you - there is evidence to the effect that -- and what or what do you say to that? All right. And then it is in the closing arguments, then we now pick it up right, the contradiction, and use them to water down the Prosecution case, et cetera. So briefly, I mean, we have instructions here from 7th of November last year. So I don't see any problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: His statement that you said correct, in the closing statement you say this or that, that's where you argue this. You said this witness said this, this witness said that, you as fact finders, you determine the credibility. However, asking this witness to comment upon what Sulejman Tihic said in his book or what Izet Izetbegovic said on the stand, that can't be done. It's for the attorneys during our final submissions to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And the Trial Chamber will --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Along the same track.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. There is a difference. You can see from the quotation you have made. I think from now on -- let's settle this point. You don't quote the evidence of another witness and ask the witness in the box to comment. All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think that is much clearer and I hope this is the last time we are discussing this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honours. Mr. Usher, we can have this excerpt from the statute, please. I don't need it in front of the witness. Next document that I have, it's a one-page document. My understanding, it's kind of specification of -- and schedule for patrolling and the duties on the roadblock, something like that. Mr. Usher, I have original in front of the witness. And put one copy on the ELMO. Could we have ID, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: ID number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D41/1 ter ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When, Mr. Fitozovic, when did this schedule, this timetable for duty -- when was it drafted?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either in the month of October or November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the title, the heading, of the document?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the timetable of duty at the points and patrols.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what are the points, the checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already explained that one was at the eastern part of the city, where one enters the Muslim and Catholic area, and at the exit point near the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My understanding, the first checkpoint was at the veterinary station, that is point number 1. Let me just see how you came to that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the second point is near the hospital, correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your capacity of committee for security?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Security committee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: SDA Security Commission?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no stamp of SDA. It doesn't say SDA. Let me say that these timetables for the checkpoints existed for duty at checkpoints from the October or November. And it's something that has been looted from my apartment. And it was carried out from the October or November of 1991, up until the beginning of aggression. And this is a document referring to the 17th of March to the 13th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, my question was: Whose commission was that you were heading?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: True, I was the president of this commission and I explained it to you what commission. And what I didn't say, you can see here in the comment here, the composition of groups can be found with the secretary of SDA and can be looked at from 8.00 to 2.00 p.m. This lady who worked at the SDA, worked professionally, and she had these office hours. These office hours. And I used her premises for working on such documents, such papers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking for the third time: Were you the President of the commission, SDA Security Commission, yes or no, Mr. Fitozovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I am answering the eighth time. I am answering yes, I was the President of the Security Commission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My conclusion is that the SDA, in connection with the patrols and these activities, had a certain type of coordination.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not the right conclusion, the one that you reached, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I'm just wondering whether it's -- the translation, but "had a certain type of coordination"? I'm sort of uncertain what you meant by that and therefore -- obviously, the witness understood what you meant because he said: "No, that's not the right conclusion." But what was it you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My question -- I can make another question with that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Or you can just answer me directly. What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What is the influence of the party SDA in this organisation of patrols and, you know, kind of surveillance or whatever, the reason for this patrolling was, what is the link between the party SDA and -- I will to clarify transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Well, it's fine. Now I understand what you meant, and you can say that and ask the witness again, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fitozovic, could we agree with the fact that SDA in Samac, militarily and otherwise, organised its patrols and other units in the period from October, 1991 to April, 1992, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic. The SDA party and the political leadership of the party did not have any influence on the creation of the patrols, the gathering of people, that were members of these patrols. I have already said a lot about this, and I do hope that I will have an opportunity to say more things about this. So what are you interested in, in a concrete way? Sulejman Tihic had nothing to do with this as the President of the Party of Democratic Action. What I did, I did, relatively speaking, on my own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you anything about Sulejman Tihic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, the witness has explained. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's move on. That's my idea. Mr. Usher, please take the document here. Mr. Usher, you can have this copy of the witness statement to give to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fitozovic, we will take a look at your statement a little bit later. Did you in a document or at a certain occasion say the following: "When the enemy occupied the entire town, the activity within it should be done in smaller groups and formations in the entire part of -- area of the town by using sabotage, assassinations, and other kinds of activities. For the completion of these tasks, it is necessary to create an engineering corps which should be well-armed with modern weapons and also equipped with motor vehicles, explosives and mines." Did you say -- do you have any knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, the quotation is fine, as far as I'm concerned, but in order to be fair to the witness, I don't think you can say to him, "Did you in a document or at a certain occasion say." I think you've got to tell him which document or on what occasion. It's a bit oblique, shall we say, to put it in that general way. So could you tell him when or in what document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. I would be more than happy to put that question with these elements but I don't know, I just have an information about the contents of certain plan or something like that, so I don't know when, how, or who, in fact, so I tried to make this inquiry with this witness, whether he is familiar with this wording and this explanations. Nothing more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: But it struck me, when you were reading, that you were doing a direct quotation, and if you've got a direct quotation, this isn't just what you are have just said now, which is you have information about the contents of a certain plan. You're giving us a direct quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but I don't have this document as such. I have only parts of certain -- I don't know, plan or whatever. So if this witness can give us the explanations whether or not he is familiar with this issues, then we can go on, and then probably we can produce something because I have certain notes from the field about these elements of maybe it's plan, maybe it's not plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe we hear from Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I've got a couple of questions. One is, the proper way of doing it is you say: "On a certain date, did you attend a meeting? At that meeting, did you say the following?" The other question I have even a step back from that is, are they asking him did he say that? Twice there was indications from Mr. Pantelic, are you familiar with this type of -- is this a theory, a military theory, that they're asking if he is familiar with this military theory or are they asking him if he ever said this? And did he say it in context of teaching maybe in 1985 how to take over a town for military offices or is this something that he said on the eve of a battle, "Here is what we are going to do"? Then you have relevance but --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is also my idea, Your Honours, to see what is the source of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, the discussion has been sufficient. If you can't identify the document, you can't identify the occasion, then you can't put it to the witness, because it's like fishing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. I'll try to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, it is hard for me to say exactly what time or where this took place but I'm asking you, did you ever, as part of the diagrams of military units that you made, which is undisputed, did you give any explanations about how these units should function, that is to say, did you maybe write such explanations?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that in some document, in a document, in the period from October, 1991 to April, 1992, you described the following thing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, before you go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If you can't identify the document or indeed the occasion, the question will not be allowed because, you see, you're trying to put into evidence matters which you, yourself, know nothing -- the source, whose source you can't identify. That's not the way you cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour, but I'm just asking a line of questions about the knowledge of this particular witness of certain areas that he covered at that time. Nothing more. I mean, if the answer would be affirmative, then we could proceed. Otherwise, I'm in the same situation almost like him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. You have to follow the correct process of cross-examination. You can't just ask questions from no where. The point is, what is your case? What is the Defence case?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. I will gladly do that, but I don't have a date, I don't have title of so-called document. I have nothing. So I have to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There is no basis for your question, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have to have this kind of explanation you know. Maybe it's a fishing expedition but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is not allowed. That is not allowed. Because we have an indictment here with a specific allegations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. Let's move to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: How much more time? Because if this type of cross-examination is continuing, I will stop you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because it seems to me that you have completed your cross-examination and all that you're doing is fishing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Your Honour, I have a couple, ten or 15 very precise questions, and we are going -- I now would like to go through his statement from 1995 and then a couple of concluding questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm giving you ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If you don't finish in ten minutes -- this is 9.40.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I beg you for another five minutes because of the so-extensive answers of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. I've given you ten minutes from now on. Let's see how your cross-examination goes. Otherwise, you stop; that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I agree absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fitozovic, could you please turn to the fourth page of your statement, in the upper right-hand corner? The last numbers are 778. I'm going to read this but you can check whether you agree with what I'm reading. The last sentence on this page: "We would usually meet at the cafe called Molla. One March night in 1992, we were sitting in Molla when, across from the cafe, a car parked, in which three Chetniks were, and they had their weapons pointing at us. Before they could shoot, our guards started shooting at them, and the three of them were severely injured." You said this to the Prosecutor in 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said to the OTP in 1995, in February. At the very beginning of my testimony, I also said that this statement was given seven years ago and the war activities were still going on at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We heard that, sir.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some parts, this statement might be a little bit subjective, but in this part here, there is nothing that can be disputed. This is exactly what I said. Maybe the difference might be that right now I wouldn't say "Chetnik," I would say "enemy." But this is just because of a time distance that had an influence on me. Therefore, right now, I would make a distinction between a Chetnik and an enemy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir. I understand you. So other than this word "Chetnik," this is all true? You stand by this statement? I'm referring to the sentence that I read out to you.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But maybe also where it says here, "our guards," it's undisputed that this was a patrol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you agree that, "The members of our patrol started shooting"?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we could not agree on that. I can tell you - but I also mentioned this in my testimony - that these were members of the reserve police corps, and I think this issue has been resolved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'm going to read to you what you said to my colleague, Pisarevic, on the 29th of May, page 8538, lines between 4 and 7. His question had to do -- was as follows. [In English] "So you did not see this incident, you only heard about it in the cafe; is that correct?" And your answer was, "Yes, and I was told who was seen and what happened."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Which incident? He was questioned about a lot of incidents. There was one where he was questioned, it sounds like he made a similar answer, about the guns being delivered on a separate occasion. Which incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we are speaking about incident on Cafe Molla. My friend from the Prosecution can turn this page and find that this is -- I'm going to ask this question about these contradictions, simply as that. Now we are speaking about the incident in Cafe Molla, obviously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fitozovic, when you answered my colleague in this manner, this is different from what you're saying now. You said to him that you weren't there, that you just heard about the event, and now you're saying that you were there. So what's the true version here?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it is true that people came up, came to kill me, and I saw these people, that's what I said. I said the same thing to Mr. Pisarevic. I saw them myself, I described the event, I described exactly what happened, that the person sitting on to the -- on the seat right next to the driver pulled down the window, and that before that, you could hear a shot fired by the driver. The driver shot into the ceiling of the car. This was done by the butcher Mesic. The other two took their automatic rifles. These were Russian-made rifles. At that moment, the members of the military police started shooting. And I also mentioned the names of these two policemen. Then the car went about 70 metres further to the junction, where Sabanovic came up to it and he took those young men to the emergency room. That's what I said, Mr. Pantelic. And now you're telling me that I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just doing my job. I have two records and I'm trying to clear things up. Please, let's not waste any time. I'm asking you for the last time, and could you please answer "yes" or "no." During this incident, this shooting incident, were you at the Cafe Molla?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. Let's move on. Page 779, those are the last three numbers on the page. This is the fifth paragraph of your statement to the OTP. Actually, this is the sixth paragraph, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you identify the page number, please, because the English is different from the B/C/S version, just identify the page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't have. It's probably due to the copying problem. Including cover page, it should be page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were saying that on the 15th of April, you got 50 automatic rifles?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did you say, 778?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 779, the sixth paragraph. You were saying that the weapons were obtained privately and that they did not come from either Croatia or Sarajevo, "We didn't receive them officially from Sarajevo. On the 16th of April, we distributed them to the braver ones. I did that publicly. I insisted on distributing the weapons in public because I wanted to create an idea of balance of power to make the Muslims and Croats feel stronger. I often wonder whether I made a mistake with this action." All right. So this is what I'm interested in. If you said that in 1995, what did you mean by this, that you often wonder whether you made a mistake? In what sense did you mean this? Would you have done something differently or something else?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will explain this to you and this thing will become clear to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain this to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wondering very often whether I made a mistake. These 50 rifles, I distributed on a public and official place at the Territorial Defence. Across the Territorial Defence, there is the building of the police of Bosanski Samac. On the first floor of the police station, everything was observed, this distribution of weapons was observed. When a member of the TO got the gun, put his name in the record, he would go to his home. That night, on the 16th, this whole event finished around 4.00 or 5.00 p.m. This distribution ended at that time. After that, at 6.00 p.m., a meeting was arranged on which Mr. Marko Bozanovic, Dragan Lukac, and Safet Hadzialijagic, nicknamed "Pop," and also representatives of other political parties, Simo Zaric from the 4th Detachment, and so on, were present. On this -- in this meeting -- well, actually, I told you already about this meeting, what was going on there, and how the meeting was ended. Simo Zaric, that is to say we actually -- we parted, and we were assured by Simo Zaric that there would be no attack and so on, but the attack did happen three hours later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We have been through this before. You don't have to repeat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Mr. Fitozovic --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, why did I think I made a mistake? I thought I made a mistake because I did this publicly. I didn't get any time by doing it publicly, and the members of the 4th Detachment and of the military, they noticed this distribution of weapons, and they just sped up the events. Maybe I also contributed to the speeding up of the events because of my distribution, of my public distribution. Maybe that is why the aggression took place that very night and not two or three nights later. That's where I made a mistake. And I still, to this day, think that that was a mistake. What happened has nothing to do with my mistake. That would have happened any way, as it happened in the entire territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fitozovic. Now we are going to page 782, that is the ERN number. Somewhere in the middle of the third paragraph, you are talking about the money for supply and that kind of thing, you had some certificates issued, and you say the following: "This money I used for people -- "

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Which page?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Again, I only have number, ERN number, in B/C/S version. It should be -- let me check. It should be eighth page, page number 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying: "This money I used for people that patrolled the streets. SDA was giving it to me. I got 1100 deutschmarks." That's what you said in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I got 1100 deutschmarks from the SDA. This money was gathered from all people that had private establishments in Bosanski Samac. So every private establishment, be it a shop or a cafe of some sort, gave a contribution so that the people that were members of the patrol could -- would have enough money to eat and have a drink somewhere. And later, also for fuel. Because we weren't getting not even a dinar from the toll that the SDS and the other patrols on the main routes were collecting, and that's where the 4th Detachment was getting its money from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am finished with this line of questions that have to do with your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, please, could I have your assistance? This is the also scheme or kind of sketch of the organisation -- structure of the unit for the defence of the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You have an original?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. I have only a copy, Your Honour. It's very, very --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The copies we have are so dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mine is also not so good but maybe the witness can clarify with us. Mr. Usher, please, could you put -- do you have a copy for the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: First could we have ID numbers, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The other problem is some words are cut off on this photocopy, on the edges, on the left and on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My copy is the same, Your Honours. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Maybe the witness can help us if he knows about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, maybe we could discuss this document for now and then we shall check within our archives and documents if we can have one better copy. And then we can submit it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fitozovic, when did this -- when was this document created?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, this for me is no document. This is the first time I see this. This may -- might be a forgery of some sort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we just have the ID number for it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: ID number, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D42/1 ter ID, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D42/1 ter ID, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My next question, Your Honours is the following:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fitozovic, is this your handwriting that's on this document, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness has said that this is the first time he has seen -- [French translation] Go on asking him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I only have to engage the forensic expert to have some, in Defence case, to have some opinions and then we shall see what is truth and what is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And you, as you said, you are going to search for the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I would be able, of course, I will search for the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Otherwise, it can't be used with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Obviously, because this witness says it's the first time that he's seeing this document. The only way for the Defence is to check all elements according to the forensic doctrine. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If they can find the original, I've got no problem faxing it to him, notifying it, sending a good copy, having him look at it again, or doing something.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My understanding, the only copy that I have at that moment. I will make some additional inquiries, see with the supporting staff in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, so we move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know who Bakir Alispahic is; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a prisoner right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he before?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was a Minister of the Police, of the republic police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What republic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you because of the transcript, Mr. Fitozovic, because we have to have everything as clear as possible. I know what you're trying to say, but because of the Judges and everybody else, we have to make sure everything is clear. I have no other intention. When was he at this position in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Pantelic, I wouldn't be able to tell you. I did not follow his work. I had my own things to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How is this relevant to Bosanski Samac, any of this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just wait. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fitozovic, do you know that Alispahic was in a car when there was a truck being unloaded with weapons in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will agree that the military organisation, Patriotic League, was founded in 1990?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard about the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I read about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge when was the Patriotic League founded?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have personal knowledge when the armed formations, Muslim armed formations, were formed, the so-called Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no personal knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did such a formation exist called the Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard that they existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you have generally heard, you know nothing specific about it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Nothing specific, as you have shown me with your hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, what is the point of all this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, link, link with the armed formation of SDA in Samac well prior the April, 1992. The link, Your Honours, and I will go through these questions, with your permission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have, Mr. Fitozovic, any knowledge that in the period March-April, 1992, vis-a-vis Bosanski Samac -- in the region of Slavonski Samac in Croatia, that over 1.000 members of the Green Berets were stationed there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you again repeat the question and the event, please? I did not follow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have, Mr. Fitozovic, personal knowledge, that in the period March-April, 1992, in Slavonski Samac, which is right across the river from Bosanski Samac, and it is located in Croatia, that it was there that over 1.000 members of well-armed Green Berets were there; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, while you were in battle operations and fighting within the HVO brigade, did you kill enemies?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When forming the armed unit in Samac, planned to kill your -- Serb inhabitants of Samac, fellow inhabitants of Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of this unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To observe the town and to protect it from those who were occupying it. I said it should be multi-ethnic and accepted by all the inhabitants of Bosanski Samac. That was the purpose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would you -- what was the purpose of this -- these weapons you had and the unit had? What would have been used?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapons of that unit were placed at the disposal of the Territorial Defence and was under the control of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was not my question. I will ask the question again. Did President SDA, Sulejman Tihic, influence you prior to your arrival to The Hague, and that you deny any connection with these organised formations, armed formations?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is no, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is AID, the secret police organisation, give you any instructions how to act and the posture to take in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also criminally charged for --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was charged and I was -- it was -- if I had to pay a fine, and it was Mr. Pisarevic who defended me on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question, my next question, has already been answered. So you did commit a criminal offence, a criminal offence?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Carried out of negligence, is my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There is a proper way of impeaching someone with a prior conviction. This isn't a proper way of doing it. I don't know the date. We don't know if these are old things, we don't know if this is a misdemeanour. If it's a misdemeanour and it goes back a long time, I would object because it wouldn't even be admissible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He will give us direct answers, Your Honour. I will just ask him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, let's shorten this. Mr. Fitozovic, can you just explain what the criminal charges if any were about?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can I lead him with the questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, let him answer from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Answer the Court, please. Why were you tried, what kind of criminal charges?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all criminal charges referred to the electric supply company in 1985-86, and on that occasion, a part, a transformer station, burned down and one of the operators was charged, as well as I, who was his head. I was defended and represented by Mr. Pisarevic, and it was treated as an act of negligence. And I had to pay a fine, a symbolic fine. And that these are the criminal charges -- all the criminal charges concerning myself in 45 years, and I don't know whether it was treated as criminal charges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, since is this is over 15 years old, it's not clear if it's a felony or a misdemeanour. It appears to be criminal negligence, so I'm assuming it's a misdemeanour. A fine was -- his sentence, apparently, or punishment, was a fine. I move that this be stricken from the record or that the Court not even consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, I disagree, Your Honour. My next question will clarify that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you agree that in 1991 you had been condemned for -- on the basis of the Article 172 of the Penal Code? And that is in 1991, not in --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Show me that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you are now discussing something else before 1991, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: 1991, yes. He was practically officially sentenced in 1991. It's not 1985. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic, for what?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For -- I will tell you. This is -- it's hard to translate. I don't know in English do we have this article. It's Article 172 of the Penal Code of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I will say it in Serbian. [Interpretation] For causing general danger. [In English] Which, in brief, is that he was sentenced for the negligence in his professional work. Then one power plant, small power plant, blown up, and there was some damage for this company that he's worked for the electrical company, and stuff like that. That's my understanding, and maybe he can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Once again, this sounds like some sort of criminal negligence. I don't even know if that's a type of felony or I would say a misdemeanour which would be recognised in countries around the world. I think it should just be deleted or stricken or just not considered, although it remains in the transcript. I think this whole thing should be stricken. It's over ten years. The incident itself occurred over 15 years, and I think it's just a waste of time here. It's irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My question, Your Honour, was not to impeach this witness with his personal background and this kind of thing because I tried --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is your point, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm going to the point now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, explain to the Chamber what is your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My point is that this witness is not telling the truth when he claimed that he was dismissed from his professional post, he was fired from the company, due to so-called ethnic problems or stuff like that. The real cause, Your Honours, was that it is not moral for the employee in the power, electric company, not to pay bills and also, if he caused certain damage by his criminal act to his company, in all jurisdictions all over the world, there are certain internal sanctions such as removal from this post to another post, stuff likes -- because the picture and the atmosphere that my learned friend from Prosecution tried to create was like this, and I want to put all this on the table. I want to clarify these things because it was not the case that he was removed from his post to another post within his company due to the ethnic -- I don't know, ethnic reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is -- number one, I don't know how he's going to prove this with this type of information. Now 2, we have a bit of a problem because it wasn't brought out by the -- by Mr. Pisarevic, who cross-examined him over two days and specifically on that, and further, Mr. Pisarevic was his legal counsel on that. So there is a problem that we might have to ask Mr. Pisarevic for certain information. And number 2, now we are getting into attorney-client privilege. We are getting into a mess here. And I think that it's -- unless he can prove, it's one thing --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If you will allow me, Your Honour, with a few questions, we will resolve this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, we discussed this at length and it is a matter you can take up in your Defence and produce the records, which I believe you have, to show that the reason for his removal from office is according to what you state.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. But allow me in my cross-examination with a certain points of my questioning to create the foundation that I will raise it -- the witness is here, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You've stated -- you've answered to colleague, my colleague, Pisarevic, for not payment of bills, that in communism it was considered immoral for people who were working in the utility company not to pay their electricity bills?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... What was considered as what, simply ask him, put it to him what you think the Defence is saying was the reason for his removal from office. It's simple.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is certain issue that I want to clarify. During the cross-examination of this witness, he said something which is not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That he said that he considered that in communism, it was not -- that the communist system -- it was immoral not to pay regular bills as an official, as a worker, of electric company, and my question is very simple: If he said that, I ask for his opinion what is his position towards the free market economy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. Mr. Pantelic, we are not going into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next question, Mr. Fitozovic, do you agree with me that you have been dismissed from your post in the Elektrodistribucija company due to the policy of the company which did not allow its employees to give a bad example to the public by not paying their bills?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a funny question, Mr. Pantelic. I believe that I already completed my answer to that question, but if I have to answer each question three times, and then you will try and find the difference between the three answers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, just answer briefly. Just give the answer briefly. Is it true that you were removed from your office because the company did not allow its employees to give a bad example to the public by not paying their bills? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next question: An additional reason for your dismissal and removal to another post, that through your criminal negligence, you caused a big loss to your company?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, on that note, maybe you could briefly find out from Mr. Fitozovic, if this alleged criminal negligence occurred in 1985 to 1986, why was -- to use your words, Mr. Pantelic, why was he condemned or found guilty and sentenced to this fine in 1991, the same year that he was dismissed from his job? It seems a big gap from 1985 to 1991. So perhaps we can just find out very briefly --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: -- why there was this big time gap. We come to 1991, obviously, a year which becomes important for our events.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is the really general matter, Your Honours. The justice is sometimes not so speedy. It's a slow process of justice. It's the first thing in general. He's not a legal expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic is nodding his head. Maybe he could respond very briefly why it took so long.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The question might be first:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fitozovic, this trial, and the entire procedure, when the transformer station burned down, when the transformer station burned, that was the case, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did that event take place? When did it burn down?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned in 1985, 1986.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The next question should only be when was it completed with the court system.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you receive the verdict?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it only from you that it was in 1991. I didn't consider it very important. It was negligence. I had to pay a fine to the amount, and the cost was of a box of cigarettes, a carton of cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And that was paid in 1991? Or you can't remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was paid within the legal framework by that date, the deadline, and I paid it. It was a symbolic sum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, Mr. Fitozovic, I think these questions could be straightened out very easily. I put a question to the witness and the question runs as follows: Was the reason for your firing in 1991, when you were dismissed and removed, your negligence in 1985 or not paying your electric bills? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, neither of the two reasons, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, when the transformer station burned down, was anybody killed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You're winding up your cross-examination now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fitozovic, can we agree that you, in cooperation with Mr. Tihic, Mr. Izet Izetbegovic, and Mr. Dragan Lukac, and others from the SDA and HDZ in Samac, in the period October-December 1991, planned an armed takeover of the government in Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Second and final question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Second and final question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Two questions. It's a two-folded question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. Second and final question. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you agree with me if I say that you have set up your own armed unit, your intelligence unit, at the end of 1991 and up to April, 1992, in close coordination with SDA and HDZ?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I finished with my questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Re-examination, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you like to take an early break and start at 5 before 11.00 or start my re-examination now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We can have a break so the witness can also rest a bit. We will take a break now and resume at five minutes before 11 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, re-examination by the Prosecution. Re-examined by Mr. Weiner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, good morning, I'd like to clarify some matters that were raised on cross-examination. Let's begin by talking about both the independent military units and Territorial Defence units which were established to defend and protect Bosanski Samac. Did you ever consult with Sulejman Tihic or any SDA party leaders concerning the operations of either unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever consult with Sulejman Tihic or SDA party leaders concerning day-to-day activities of either unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you consult with Sulejman Tihic or SDA party leaders in relation to the staffing of the unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, did you consult with those same persons in relation to the assignment of personnel for either unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you consult with the HDZ party leaders concerning any of those matters I just mentioned: operations, day-to-day activities, staffing, assignments of personnel, of either unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you consult with the party leaders?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, here I must explain the following. That is why, in fact, I had been invited. Throughout my activity from October 1991 -- from September, 1991, to the beginning of the aggression, the 17th of April, 1992, throughout that time, all the time I was fleeing and avoiding Sulejman Tihic, or I didn't allow him to come close to me in the sense that he would be giving certain suggestions concerning the forming of the -- this unit which was, in fact, already formed. Why did I do that? The reasons are the following: Mr. Tihic was, from the first days of this period under observation -- relevant period, from September, 1991, until the aggression, had contact with certain structures of the state security service in Doboj, where Simo Zaric was employed. Therefore, I didn't believe him in this sense. Next, I avoided the possibility of giving party connotations to that unit. In the party, Mr. Izet Izetbegovic was present and Sulejman Tihic represented -- presented to the public during this period as a person who had a penchant for alcohol consumption, which is not true, but it is something that was left in the public domain. Therefore, when forming these units, I was avoiding also Izet Izetbegovic. Throughout this testimony of mine, it's clear that this unit belonged neither to the Green Berets, nor to the unit of the Patriotic League. As a child who grew up in Bosanski Samac, and as I say grew up there, where everybody knew me, be it Serbs, Croats and Muslims, I wished to form such a unit which would defend Bosanski Samac against all occupying forces. And even if Bosanski Samac were endangered by Muslim fundamentalism, I, in my capacity of organiser of the unit, I would fight also against such ideas. However, I did have the support of moral support - not professional but moral support - of many reserve officers, be it Serbs, Muslims or Croats, who were really -- who wanted to join the Territorial Defence but such a defence which would have no links with the party SDA or any other political party. In that sense, that unit was formed. So no -- it didn't belong to any other armies or have links with any other parties. And that is why Sulejman Tihic, I avoided him, and I didn't allow him to have closer contacts with me. Because of those characteristics in which he painted Izet Izetbegovic, I would avoid also Izet Izetbegovic, in order to have around me as many people as possible who were not under the political influence of a party or under some other political influence. This is as far as your question is concerned, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue on with those -- with the first unit, the -- your private, if you want to call it, your private military unit. You testified that, in March, members who were working the patrols began being paid; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also testified that the SDA gave you some money for that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The party gave me 1100 deutschmarks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did other persons give you money for the unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All people that owned a private enterprise of some sort in the city of Bosanski Samac gave me some financial help so that these young men could be ensured to receive food, fuel and so on. These were all very symbolic amounts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you receive the most -- most of the money or the majority of the funds? From the SDA or from the private businesses?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the private businesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Fitozovic, you say that this private funding came from, to quote you, "all people." Could you tell us whether "all people" refers to all ethnic groups or not, as the case might be, who owned these private businesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could say that this included members of all ethnic groups except the Serbs. There were only one or two such cases. As far as Croats are concerned, those that had some kind of a business in Bosanski Samac, I got their participation of 100 per cent. And maybe about 90 per cent of the Muslims that owned these private businesses were also supporting us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's continue on with the Territorial Defence unit. Were all citizens in Bosanski Samac invited to join the Territorial Defence unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was a public invitation and everybody was invited.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that include Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Members of the SDS party, does that include them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Not the SDS. All the Serbs that did not belong to political parties, or if they belonged to the SDS party privately, they could still also register with the TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you publicly invited members of the 4th Detachment to join the Territorial Defence unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the meeting that took place on the 16th of April, at 6.00 p.m. - the defendant Zaric was also there - I invited the 4th Detachment members to join the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you showed us some of your plans that you had made for the certain units that you had, the anti-sabotage unit, the medical unit, the communications unit. Do you recall showing us those plans?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you indicated previously that those had been drafted on or about April 13th and 14th of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after April 13th and 14th, did you continue to go out and get new members for the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go look for them. They were coming themselves to the offices of the Territorial Defence and they volunteered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these people who volunteered on the 15th and 16th, were there members of the -- were any of those people Croats and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were Croats and Serbs among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there members of the 4th Detachment that were recruited or that voluntarily joined on April 15th and 16th, after you had completed those unit plans?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment when the plans were made, there were no members of the 4th Detachment, but they did register with the Territorial Defence. The dilemma was just how to register their weapons that they received from the 4th Detachment, and this was a question that I posed to Zaric on the meeting that happened on the 16th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But the fact that these people registered after you had drafted your plans, Serbs, Croats, members of the 4th Detachment, were you intending to modify or revise those units based on these new additions to the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We had such plans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, why didn't you in fact revise or modify those initial plans?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't do it because the aggression happened on the 17th of April, after midnight. So we had no opportunity to consolidate all these units and the names and specialties and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Getting away from that, you testified very briefly that Radovan Karadzic visited Bosanski Samac. Do you recall when that occurred?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was in December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this a speech or did he just take a tour of the area? What did he do when he got there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came to hold a political speech and also to make preparations for the creation of the Serbian municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the defendants present with him or when he spoke?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
