utterances.text: Which defendants were with him?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blagoje Simic was there of the defendants. I can't say anything about the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this at the speech that Blagoje Simic was there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while Blagoje Simic, the defendant, was there, what do you recall Radovan Karadzic said about Bosanski Samac, the creation of a Serbian municipality? What did he say?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I can't quote verbatim what Radovan Karadzic said. I had said earlier that in this meeting, the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac was supposed to be formed and also its boundaries, its borders, should have been established, to determine what territory this Serbian municipality would encompass. Those were mainly the town of Samac, all the villages with Serb population, and Croatian villages, Zasavica, Tisina, Donji Hasic, Gornji Hasic, Novo Selo, Tursinovac, and also a part of Grebnice, and Kornica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Radovan Antic explain, while the defendant Blagoje Simic was present, how this conversion was supposed to take place where Bosanski Samac was going to change from a municipality run by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Radovan Karadzic explain how the municipality of Bosanski Samac was going to suddenly be converted to Serbian Samac? Did he explain that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He explained it in the following way. First of all, this had to be done with political negotiations, including other political parties that existed in Bosanski Samac, but if this could not be done in such a way, then a date would be set as a condition when these parties would have to agree with the formation or the -- with the formation of the municipality of Srpski Samac. After that, in the same place, Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic, the commander of the 17th Tactical Group, said, "We will be in blood up to your knees here." This is what he said word for word.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the defendant present when Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic said that, "We would be up to our knees in blood," [Realtime transcript read in error "your knees"] or "We will be in blood up to our knees here"? When a statement along those lines was made, was the defendant Blagoje Simic present?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blagoje Simic was not present. Simo Zaric was present then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when Radovan Karadzic made his statement about converting Bosanski Samac into a Serbian Bosanski Samac, was the defendant Blagoje Simic present? And where they said the parties will have to agree by a certain date, was the defendant present?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: On page 45, line 11, the witness said, "After that, in the same place, Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic, the commander of the 17th Tactical Group said, "We will be in blood up to your knees here." There is some confusion there. Who is "we" and who is "you"? "We will be in blood up to your knees here." What is the meaning behind that statement? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Please answer the Judge's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see Mr. Lazarevic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm not objecting to the line of examining by Mr. Weiner but I believe the witness was talking about two events, and if my learned colleague could clarify was Mr. Colonel Nikolic present when Radovan Karadzic was speaking or he was talking -- because he was talking only about the same place, not about same time. Because I am a bit confused, is he talking about one event or two separate events?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner? You can clarify that with the witness and also let the witness answer the question from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first question, sir: Were you referring to two meetings which occurred in December at that same location, one with the defendant Blagoje Simic, and Radovan Karadzic, and a second meeting with Colonel Nikolic and the defendant Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was talking about two events that took place, one after the other, but they both took place in the same location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just two brief questions: Which one occurred first and what was the time period between the two events?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, Radovan Karadzic arrived, and shortly thereafter, the meeting was held in the memorial centre, where Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic was present. And now I can also answer the Judge's question. This might be a problem with the interpretation, but what I said is the following: In this meeting, Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic, considering everything that was going on in the town and surrounding the town, said, verbatim, "Here," meaning the town of Bosanski Samac, "There will be blood up to the knee level." That is what he said. "They," that is to say those who will not do what he wants from them, "Those people will have blood up to their knees."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's talk about some of the documents that were shown to you by Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I was very curious to follow this line of examination, and I didn't object at the beginning. Number 1, my belief that the re-direct cannot be conducted as such because these events, these names, were never mentioned in cross-examination. My learned friend from the Prosecution was in situation during examination-in-chief to find out everything about these events after the certain part of statement of this witness. He failed to do that. None of the Defence counsel in cross-examination never raised that issue. However, this was very interesting statement, although it's a fact that it's not true, of course, but that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm objecting. This is just a speech by counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's a matter of principle, Your Honour. If this line of questioning in re-direct will be allowed, then I think that Defence counsel, Defence team, should be allowed for the limited issue to go to re-cross, because of the well-known standards that we have here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, with regard to Radovan Karadzic, that issue got raised on cross-examination while Mr. Pisarevic cross-examined this witness. I was surprised that he started to mention it, that not only was there a meeting at the local commune or the memorial hall involving Colonel Nikolic but there was another meeting involving Radovan Karadzic. Since they brought the testimony out, what I'm allowed to do on re-direct examination is to clarify, modify, further explanation, and also examine issues which are raised on cross-examination. Since they opened the issue, since they opened the door, I'm allowed to follow in, and that's exactly what I'm doing here. They've raised the issue. I've briefly gotten out -- I've briefly introduced through this witness or I've just asked questions about this witness about something that was said on cross-examination. And that's all I've done, which is proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please to the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour it would be appropriate that my colleague would respond because I was not mentioned in this context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But Mr. Pantelic, Mr. Weiner has accepted and the Trial Chamber is of the view that the Prosecution is in order. That's it. Mr. Pisarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just with regard to what my learned colleague of the Prosecution has said, I have never asked a question in my cross-examination that had to do with a meeting where Radovan Karadzic was present. To my question why Mr. Fitozovic did not respond to his call-up, because he was supposed to go together, he said the following, "How can I respond to the call-up because Radovan Karadzic was in Samac in December?" This is the only time the witness mentioned Radovan Karadzic being in Samac and I did not ask any further questions about this in my cross-examination, and I don't think this is a basis for this kind of questioning to be pursued because I never asked the witness anything about the presence of Radovan Karadzic in Samac. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the witness said further that recruitment of Muslims and Croats were affected after Radovan Antic -- I'm sorry, Radovan Karadzic spoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And that is page?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I will get the page, if you want. I'm sorry, I didn't bring it with me. We've had five days of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber is of the view that the Prosecution is in order to re-examine along the lines that Mr. Weiner has taken because the record is clear as to what issues were raised during cross-examination by the Defence. Mr. Weiner, you can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just prior to the objection, we were moving on to discuss some of the documents and I'd like to briefly discuss a few of the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to try and do this to speed things up and see if we can do that without having you examine the documents again, but just refer to them because I think some of them you were very familiar with. You were shown document P67 ter ID which is -- and there was a similar document, D50/3 for ID, and if you recall, P67 was the one that you swam -- you put in a plastic bag and swam over the river with. And P50 was the one that you claim to be a forgery. Why do you believe that D50/3 for ID, that document was a forgery or had a forged signature? Please tell the Court why you believe it to be a forgery.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can claim it with certainty, for the command, town command, I didn't consider myself competent to sign that document, nor did I have the stamp. In the SDA party, nobody had the competence to sign this document. They were in doubt who should sign that document. And below it, you had neither the names of Tihic nor of Izet Izetbegovic or anybody else. As I remember, it's the city board of SDA. There was the stamp. And that was the original which I took and I swam across. There is no dilemma about that. And it is -- there is no dilemma that it was a forged signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, at page 50, line 10, it says P50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the one you claim was a forgery, why do you believe D50/3, it should read not "P50" but "D50," "D" as in "dog."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, it's P50. It should be D50/3?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, D50/3 is the one that he claims to be a forgery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just very briefly, you were shown a newspaper clipping from Oslobodenje concerning some prisoner exchanges in 1991. Do you recall that, first, being shown by Defence counsel that newspaper article?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had you ever seen that newspaper article previously?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Yesterday, I saw it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that newspaper article, which discussed the exchanges in 1991 in Bosanski Samac, concerned exchanges of prisoners of war, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The article spoke of the exchange of POWs, prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was nothing in that article about exchanges involving civilians and women and children and elderly, was there, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could move on, could the witness be shown document "D" as in "dog" 34/1 ID ter?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I clarify that this is indeed D34/1? It was admitted yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, on -- during cross-examination, you admitted that you had drawn or drafted that document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I drafted that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you indicated that there was an accompanying document of text which was missing?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is only a part of this document, and the text is missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since the text is missing, please tell the Court why was that document drafted and what does it concern?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document refers to the -- in case of outbreak of war and war operations, and the instruction contains when and if this will be implemented at all, this, what is drawn here on this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And please tell us what is it a plan to do? What were you going to do?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This plan included the building on the left side, you can see, a part of CCA 300 metres of long distance transmission lines, and that had to be built in view of the fact that this transformer station, Batkusa, was located in a Serbian -- in a Serb village close to Obudovac, where the paramilitary units were stationed. So these were units which arrived from Serbia and so on. It was to be assumed that the electricity supply would be cut off near Domaljevac. So here where you can see Brvnik, Domaljevac, this is the long distance transmission line, carrying electricity to the Croatian village of Domaljevac. And here you can see the construction of this long distance transmission line which had to be erected so that the Croatian villages of Domaljevac, Grebnice, Tursinovac, Novo Selo, could be supplied with electricity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you place it on the ELMO and please show the Court what you're referring to? Let me ask you just a simple question without getting into all this electrical technology. Were you going to cut or destroy the power line that went to the Serb paramilitaries, to stop the power from going to the Serb paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But in the text, it was also written when that would be carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you just show the Court what you were referring to, the power stations and things?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This transformer station was in the Serbian village of Batkusa and it supplied electric power Brvnik, Slatina, Obudovac. These were all local communes with a Serb population. And from this station, electricity was also supplied to Domaljevac, Grebnice, Tursinovac, Croat villages. So in addition to the destruction in this area, what was planned was to erect long distance transmission line, and this to the approximately 300 metres. Or to be quite precise, what it's all about: In case the power was cut, in this transformer station, so that Domaljevac and other Croat villages would remain without electricity, in that case, we -- this would be toppled and cut here so that the power supply wouldn't flow towards the transformer station, and nobody would have electricity. Here, you can see the building as well as the severing, the cutting. The destruction was foreseen at a later stage if electricity would be cut off for the Croat villages, then in that case, the destruction would take place. That is what contained that text, and which is missing here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was your plan to cut power to the JNA and the paramilitaries and, if power was further cut to the villages, you were going to reconnect it with some sort of 300 metre line? Is that basically what you were planning to do?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically, the plan was, if the Serbs cut off electricity supply to Domaljevac, here the destruction would take place towards these Serb villages. So this was linked. Therefore, in -- if in Batkusa the electricity is cut, will cut off electricity for the Croat villages, then electricity supply would be cut off to the Serb villages, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Does the Court have any questions on that document before we move on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You can remove that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were questioned by counsel, Mr. Pantelic, about an indication or a statement within your ten page statement or nine page statement, a comment you made within your nine page statement, where you admitted saying something to Simo Zaric which was a lie or an exaggeration. Now, in a court of law, you swear to tell the truth. In wartime or a pre-war situation, is deception used when dealing with an enemy?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, when I said "lie," I told the truth in my statement. It was a lie in the sense of tactics, because also the defendant stated there would be no conflict. He stated that at the meeting. But it occurred two or three hours later. That was also a lie. So it's all within the framework of a military -- of military tactics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you said the defendant said that, you were referring to Simo Zaric lying at that same meeting on April 16th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, moving on, you were questioned about the incident at the Cafe Molla. When that vehicle arrived, where were you? Where were you situated?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was within Cafe Molla, inside, directly vis-a-vis the automobile, the vehicle. I saw the entire length of the vehicle and everything that was happening five metres in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you seated inside?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when the shooting started, did you drop to the floor or did you run outside? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, all of us fell to the floor, once there was the burst of fire. And I just raised my head and saw that the vehicle moved to the right. Then I went out and I could see where the vehicle stopped, some 70 metres further down from this cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And having dropped to the floor, were there portions of the incident that you were unable to see?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I had seen everything except those patrols which were outside. I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, during this six to seven month period that you had that independent police -- that independent military unit, other than this incident where someone tried to assassinate you or had plans to assassinate you and there was a shooting, was there any other incident involving shootings in relation to your unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would ask you to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure. We just talked about this incident which occurred late March, early April, this shooting incident that had occurred that you just testified about at the Cafe Molla. Other than that one incident, during the six to seven month period that you had your independent military unit, were there any other shootings or incidents involving violence, relating to your unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During the course of these six months, particularly at the beginning of 1992, from January to April, there was a lot of shooting in town, in the different neighbourhoods of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were any of these shootings involving your military unit? Were they out shooting, were they involved in any of these shootings?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. They were never there shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the only incident involving your military unit was that incident that occurred at the Cafe Molla?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One couldn't put it that way. In that incident, this unit did not participate, this independent unit did not participate in that incident. The parties involved in the incident were members of the 4th Detachment and the members of the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, your independent military unit was never involved in a shooting incident in a six to seven month period; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it never participated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, there was some discussion at the end of cross-examination concerning your termination of employment in 1991. Have you ever received a notice of your termination of employment from the electrical power plant?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you receive that notice?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received it a month ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your notice of termination in 1991 was received almost 11 years later?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that there was an incident in 1985, 1986, where a power station or a power line had burnt?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, all the years after that, 1987 through the end of 1991, after that incident of the power line, did you continue to serve as a supervisor over 52 people or 52 employees at that company?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From that event to the 24th of December, 1991, I was working and occupying the same position. I was supervisor of the technical operations unit with 52 workers. So within the company, I wasn't disciplined, nor was I replaced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your current position, are you currently working in a similar position as a supervisor of a power plant?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now I am director of the electrical supply company, Domaljevac Samac, Domaljevac unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fitozovic, for giving your evidence at the Tribunal. You're now finished and you can go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The witness left his bag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness left his bag, Mr. Usher. Yes, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wanted to utilise this break concerning the yesterday's motion of the Prosecution. I also wanted to introduce the official translations of certain documents. I don't know shall we do it now, prior to the introduction of the next witness, or at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Since you have the documents ready with you, can we have them?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I prepared two documents. One is the document on which we dwelt last week. It was D40/3. The problem which arose was the B/C/S version was one-sheet document and the translation had two pages. Also, the B/C/S version, in fact, had only one page translated. I also -- it was a document we introduced with the witness Mehinovic Kemal. Now, this has the identification as D40/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. We have now got the entire translation and the complete documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's a complete document in the B/C/S version, and a complete translation. I would tender it as evidence because up until now it had only the ID number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any objection from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think the Prosecution find themselves in an unusual position because -- I appreciate that what happened was of course no design whatsoever on behalf of the Defence but we did not receive the second page of this document until now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you need time to look at it?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. What flows from that, though, is that -- I was advised last week that there was a second page to it. It's just that now we have actually been handed this. So that that's not my problem about time, but the issue remains that we had first objected on a number of grounds, one of them being that this document had no source or signature or anything like that. That element now is somewhat mitigated because we can see, on the second page, a name and a signature. So we can see who purported -- who purports to be the author of this document. However, this document as it stands now was not put to the witness, either, indeed, Kemal Mehinovic, through whom this was originally discussed, or I think the following witness also discussed it. He was a protected witness, Witness E. And just in terms of the name, the commander, it was not exactly the same document that was put to them. So I feel it may be a little bit inappropriate now to make it a full document in evidence when in fact the witness, at the time when it was discussed and everything, only had knowledge of and discussed the first page and did not discuss the complete document. And in fact, as it happened, neither witness had ever seen this document or was able to assist on any clarification about the nature of this document. Any information about it came purely from counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I appreciate it's nothing to do with -- unfortunately, there was nothing, as I said, by design by my learned colleague on Defence but I do feel we would not be happy at this stage, it being full evidence until we have some witness who --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We would not be happy having it admitted fully into evidence until we have some witness who can at least see the whole document, perhaps shed some light on it and answer some questions, with the full document being available to the Bench and to the witness and to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Lukic, I think the Trial Chamber agrees with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully agree. My learned colleague has already informed me that this would be the position of the OTP. I would just like to remind everybody that the document I received is a part of the Tribunal file, of the court file, in Bijeljina, and I'm going to prove the authenticity of the entire document during the Defence case, and I don't think this will be a problem in my case. But, for now, I agree that this document should only keep an ID number. The second document is D16/3 ter ID. I have also received an official translation in the meantime for this document. This was a protected witness, and therefore I would like to ask that his name not be mentioned in our discussion. The verdict of the supreme military court, May 31, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, we have the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think if the Prosecution has no objections, I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, we were unaware that this was going to be moved into evidence today so we would just like to check that there was no other outstanding issue apart from the translation. If that is the only outstanding matter, of course, we have is no objection but I would just like to say we can inform you immediately after the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Later, okay. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further documents. I would only like to use this opportunity, Your Honours, to say that if the Defence is required to say something about the proposal made yesterday by the Prosecution that Kemal Bobic be asked to testify, that it is the position of the Defence - and I'm talking about on behalf of all the Defence counsel - it is our position that we object or oppose to this proposal, and I can say it now, something about what my learned colleague Weiner said yesterday, but if it is necessary to submit a written document, then we can do that later. But the issue is whether the Prosecution needs to add more to what Mr. Weiner said yesterday or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But what is the basis of your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is what the objection is about. It has to do both with legal and factual things. First of all, there are two defences here that have to do with reciprocal disclosure and, therefore, we were supposed to receive everything from the Prosecution before. Second of all, it is clear that in accordance with 73 bis(D) the Prosecutor can, after the beginning of the trial, if they deem it necessary, and if it is in the interests of justice, submit a request to again accept the original list of witnesses. In this concrete case, the facts are as follows: In the Pre-Trial Conference, the Trial Chamber suggested to the OTP to reduce the list, the number of witnesses. Based on this suggestion - and this was not a decision - the OTP, in its brief of July 6th, gave -- did not -- decided not to call the witness Kemal Bobic and some other witnesses. Now the OTP is suggesting to call this witness, and the explanation being that he was -- this would be a cumulative testimony as well as Esad Cosic, who was already on the list relating to the same facts, and also that this was -- this would enable the testimony of Ediba Bobic, who is in poor health. On the other hand, Esad Cosic will not be talking about the same things as Kemal Bobic. They were detained in different institutions. Kemal Bobic was in Batkovic until 1994, and his testimony is cumulative and has to do with the -- with the testimonies of witnesses that had already testified and those are also some of the people that were exchanged with him. On the other hand, the health of Ediba Bobic could not be in the interest of justice and be cause for a witness to be called. If this health situation is so bad, this could not be the reason for this man to be called to witness -- to testify, especially because she was only suggested under the Rule 92 bis and it is an issue whether she will be called at all. But in the interests of justice, the Trial Chamber can allow for another witness to be called. The interest of justice is here totally on the side of the defendants, because from July 6 onwards, the statement of this witness from a previous trial was put ad acta. And now there are efforts to again call a completely new witness and in this way limit the rights from the Article 21 of the Statute, and the reasons which are being named by the Prosecution have nothing to do with the interests of justice. Therefore, I think that this could not be put into any relation with Omer Nalic and Ibro Taletovic that the Prosecution will not call, because those are only reasons that are known to the Prosecution why they decided not to call these witnesses. And this witness is going to be providing cumulative evidence, that is the same as the evidence of the witnesses that have already been called. Therefore, the Defence does not agree with the suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will consider the matter and make a ruling at a later stage. Can we have the next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe the defendants could exchange places in accordance with your procedures?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The defendants can change places. Yes. That has been done.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Also on this matter which we just discussed, the Prosecution is a little bit taken aback because the indication that we got from the Defence when we first raised this matter with them was a completely different position from what we've just heard. So I would like to take the opportunity to just file a written document in response, a short, brief one, setting out our position as to why we want to call this witness and our complete circumstances, because I think that now, in light of what we've heard, which was, as I said, not what we were expecting from the Defence, that we would just like to make our position and all the facts clear to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Then you may put in a written motion.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness can be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Yes, the Prosecution, examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Examined by Ms. Reidy:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could I ask you to state your full name for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Jelena Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell the Court your date and place of birth?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on April 4th, 1957, in Gradacac, in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Gradacac is in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then I understand that your family in fact come from Slavonski Samac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My family has been living in Croatia for a long time, although they originally come from Bosnia. However, they have been living in Croatia for many years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you yourself are of Croatian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you spend your childhood in Slavonski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I spent my entire childhood up until 1977 in Slavonski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1977, where did you move to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You said you spent your entire childhood until 1977 in Slavonski Samac. And then after you left Slavonski Samac, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I started secondary school in Osijek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Osijek is also in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Osijek is also in Croatia. I have a remark. There is an error regarding this year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You can correct it for us.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I lived in Slavonski Samac until 1972. That's when I left Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So not 1977, but you left Slavonski Samac in 1972?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After attending secondary school in Osijek in Croatia, did you then move to Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I lived in Bosanski Samac in the meantime as well as a student, as an intern.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you were in Bosanski Samac as an intern, where was the place of your study?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a catering school in Osijek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you marry in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I married in Bosanski Samac in 1973.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the name of your husband who you married in 1973?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: His name was Slobodan Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which ethnicity was he?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: My husband was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was your husband from Bosanski Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was from Bosanski Samac municipality, from Donja Slatina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand, then, that your first husband, Slobodan Stanisic, he died in 1989; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, my husband died that year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you continue to use his surname up until you remarried?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I had no reason to change my last name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in 1992, did you go by the name of Jelena Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After you finished your studies in Osijek and you said they were for a catering course, did you then work in Bosanski Samac for some time?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you working in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I worked at the hotel Plaza in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your job at the hotel?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I was a receptionist for a longer time, and then later, I opened up a tourist bureau and I worked there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these two professions bring you in contact with a lot of people in the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, with a lot of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you still in this job in 1992 or had you stopped working?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No. That year, I wasn't working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just for the record, when exactly did you stop working?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that by your own choice?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In -- I'm going to talk about now 1992. In 1992, were you living in the apartment which you had shared with your husband Slobodan Stanisic in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was still living in that apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you there by yourself or were you living with your current husband, Mr. Kapetanovic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, my boyfriend and I were living together in my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Kapetanovic, which ethnic background does he hold?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: He is Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to ask you now about people from Bosanski Samac, and the first person is a Dr. Blagoje Simic. Do you know Dr. Blagoje Simic from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I had a chance to see him, and I was also his patient once or twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know anything -- did you know whether or not he was politically active?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what exactly did you know about his political activity?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I knew that he was politically very active, that he was one of the leaders of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which political party he was associated with?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Kapetanovic, could I ask you to look around the courtroom today and if you see the Blagoje Simic that you just described to the courtroom, could you please tell the Court where he's sitting?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Blagoje Simic, that is to say Dr. Simic, is sitting on my left, towards the windows. He is the first next to the policeman who is on my right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the record could reflect that Mr. Simic has been correctly identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now turn to it a second gentleman by the name of Miroslav Tadic. Are you familiar with Miroslav Tadic from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I tried to understand when I reading this transcript. Could the witness, with a more specific details, can describe Mr. Blagoje Simic? Otherwise, you know, window, left, right, guards, it's a little confusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That was understood by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can proceed, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, I asked you about a Miroslav Tadic. Are you familiar with a Miroslav Tadic from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know Mr. Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court whether you know him well or not, and if so, how well you know him?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: We weren't family friends but we knew each other quite well. By this, I mean that I had the opportunity to see him quite frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have any contact with him whilst you were operating this tourist agency?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I also had an opportunity to see him there, and I am also referring to the high school location, considering the fact that Miroslav Tadic worked there. I went by his office quite frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Miroslav Tadic used to work at the high school and you went to his office quite frequently. What caused you to go to his office at this time when he was working in the high school?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, I cooperated with everybody, and I also worked at the high school. I mean professional cooperation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it like organising school tours and trips and things like that? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, could I ask you to look around this courtroom and if you see the Miroslav Tadic you've been talking about here today, then describe to the bench where he's sitting.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Yes. I know where he's sitting. He is sitting in the same row, right next to Dr. Blagoje Simic. So if I'm looking at them from the right, first the guard is sitting, then Blagoje Simic, and then Mr. Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. I think the record can reflect the identification of Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, finally, a third person I'd like to ask you about is Simo Zaric. Do you know Simo Zaric from Bosanski Samac, and if you do, could you just explain the context in which you know Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know Mr. Simo Zaric from Bosanski Samac. I know him as a businessman and also as my neighbour. I mean my former neighbour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you know him as a businessman, what -- what employment was he in at the time when you knew him as a businessman?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, I know him because of the fact that I worked as a receptionist, and I had to report all the foreigners to the police. So he was the chief of the SUP. And then I also know him from an entirely different area. Across from my street, he worked at the company called Buducnost.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And as with the other two gentlemen we spoke about, if you see Mr. Zaric here today, just advise the Bench where he's sitting.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Yes. I see Mr. Simo Zaric here. He's sitting first on -- from my left. So starting with the policeman, he is sitting right between the policeman and Mr. Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. And if the record could just reflect the identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, you've just told the Court that Simo Zaric, you also knew as your neighbour. Where were you living exactly in April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I lived in Bosanski Samac, in Edvard Kardelj Street, in a building, S62, entrance 2, apartment number 16.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say Simo Zaric was your neighbour, did he also have an apartment in this block?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said he was my neighbour. Mr. Simo Zaric lived in the same street, in the same building, but in the fourth entrance.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a diagram drawn up to instruction of the witness, just of her apartment block and the house and entrance. This has been in issue before, and there is other uses I'd like to make of this diagram, particularly events pertaining to the night of the 17th of April, but it may be useful now if I just ask the witness to identify where her house is and where she said the defendant's apartment is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: These diagrams have been disclosed to Defence counsel. I also have copies for the Bench here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, do you recognise the diagram that's on the screen in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is a diagram of the building that I lived in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could I ask you to take a pen, which is, for the record, it will be easier -- perhaps I could ask the usher if there is a thinner pen, a blue pen, in the holder -- on it, there is a number of -- could I ask you to mark -- I see there is a number 2 marked beside entrances to that building. Is that the entrance to your apartment block?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Put an "A" just beside that.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the entrance to your building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just place a "B" beside the entrance to Simo Zaric's building?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's sufficient for the moment. Perhaps we can just leave this beside the witness because we will come back to, or if the Bench prefers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number of the diagram?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be P68 ID, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, my colleague has drawn the attention -- my attention to the fact that it's 12.30, and I understand that's the scheduled time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We shall have a break until 10 minutes before 1.00, that is 12.50 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, examination-in-chief continuing.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, before the break, you marked on a diagram where the entrance to your apartment was in the block 62 and where the entrance to Simo Zaric's apartment was in block 62. Did you have a good observation, or could you well observe people who were coming and going into that entrance which led to Simo Zaric's apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I could observe for two reasons. The entrance -- my entrance is close to the entrance of Mr. Simo Zaric, and my living-room windows were on the same side where Simo Zaric's entrance was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And in the month or so leading up to the 17th of April, 1992, did you observe any increase in the amount of visitors or the types of people coming to visit Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I noticed that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber what exactly you observed?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I observed an increased amount of visitors on that entrance, the movement of people who were members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any of the defendants in this case going to visit Mr. Simo Zaric? That would be either Blagoje Simic or Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did observe that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe both of them or either one of them?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I observed them a number -- rather frequently. I cannot say whether they were coming together but they were arriving frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did see both Blagoje Simic and Miroslav Tadic going into the apartment, the entrance of the apartment --

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: In fact, that is what my question was going to be, Ms. Reidy. I presume that we are going to find out not only that the witness saw Mr. Simic and Mr. Tadic going into the entrance of the apartment, but we also would need to know did she see them go into the actual apartment of Mr. Simic, and if so, how.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour, I'm going to follow that point up. And just for the record, I'm correcting Your Honour but I think you mean the apartment of Mr. Zaric. It's just line 16 of the -- of page 74.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Which line?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry, line 16, page 74. I think it was just a slip of the tongue to refer to the apartment of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Exactly, a slip of the tongue. I meant the apartment of Mr. Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's what I understood you to mean, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, could you tell the Chamber did you see these persons enter the entrance which led to Mr. Zaric's apartment or did you actually see them enter Mr. Simo Zaric's apartment itself?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I must say that I only saw them entering the entrance number 4, but I -- that I did not see them enter the apartment of Mr. Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it you never followed any of these people when they went up into entrance number 4?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I never did that. There were -- was never any need for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is the reason that you believe that they were visiting Mr. Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, calling for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, it's not speculation. I'm asking the witness to explain her answer, to give her reasons for her belief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: She has already said that, that she believed that they were visiting Mr. Zaric. Did she say that?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I believe she said that on the record, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because all we have is the identification of the entrance to Mr. -- it's a common entrance, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour, then I'll ask --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, you've testified that you never followed these visitors once they went past the entrance. Where do you believe that they went after they entered entrance number 4?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that I know these gentlemen, that they are good friends and members of the same party, of the same unit, it was quite logical to me that they were going visiting Mr. Simo Zaric, because the other inhabitants living there, dwellers, were not as interesting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Miss Reidy, again, if you could maybe clarify or find out from the witness which floor, first of all, her apartment was on; secondly, what floor, or did she know the floor that Mr. Simo Zaric's apartment was on? And thirdly, whether it was possible, if she was looking out of her window, to see not only the entrance to block number 4, where Mr. Zaric's apartment was, but whether she would be able to see from her window through his window anyone in the room or rooms.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, perhaps you could answer those questions in exactly the order Her Honour asked them. Could you please first tell the Chamber on which floor of your section of the apartment block your apartment was located?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My apartment was located -- first we have the ground floor, first floor, second floor. I was the third, on the third level, although it was the second floor. The apartment of Mr. Simo Zaric was on the fourth entrance. I don't know the apartment number, but if we take into consideration that we begin with ground floor, he was on the third floor, but it was the fourth landing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I understand, then, that he was -- his apartment would have been one level higher than yours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe it is correct. I must also add that I never visited Mr. Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have any sort of view at all from your apartment, the living-room window you described, into any of the rooms of Mr. Simo Zaric's apartment? Would you have been able to observe any meeting going on there?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I never did this. I never looked in the direction of the floors of Mr. Zaric's apartment except for the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just to be clear, you saw, amongst others, Miroslav Tadic and Blagoje Simic come to the apartment block known as 62 Edvard Kardelj and go into the fourth entrance which leads to, amongst others, Mr. Simo Zaric's apartment? Is that a correct analysis of what you've testified so far?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It is quite a correct analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have any conversations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I have a question, straight to the witness: Could you repeat more in detail who were the persons, other persons or families living in the same entrance as Mr. Simo Zaric on the different floors? Can you explain -- tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. At this point in time, I cannot remember. Even at this point, I cannot remember the names of my neighbours from the third entrance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: From the fourth entrance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But I stated that I cannot remember the names of those who were even closer to me, because ten years have passed since then, and I wasn't interested in these people any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, did you ever, at the time, talk to any of your other neighbours, maybe from your block or any other blocks, about whether or not they had noticed what you describe as an increase of visits from people going into entrance number 4 and was there any discussion about things that were happening in -- what people believed to be happening in Mr. Zaric's apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite frequently. This was very topical issue at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So could you please clarify for us what sort of things people were commenting upon and then also with whom or which people were noticing the things that you've described?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Most of the commentaries I could hear from my neighbours living at the same entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you just give us an example of the sort of commentaries that your neighbours, and you or your neighbours, would make to each other in noticing what was going on?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was the time of great political strife among the various nationalities so that they would attract as many followers as possible. We also knew -- I knew that the previously mentioned names, that they belonged to the party SDS. I also knew that these three persons were closely attached to the detachment that was known as 4th Detachment. Similarly, we had the tenants who were from other parties, SDA, and it was logical that verbally they also speculated, and big discussions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it correct to say that the increase of visitors to entrance number 4 and the particular persons who were coming to that entrance gave rise to certain discussion as to what was occurring, everybody believed to be occurring in Mr. Zaric's apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was precisely like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to ask you about another location in Bosanski Samac. Are you familiar with the Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I would like to put a question to the witness. When you told us that there were discussions and perhaps rumours because of the traffic into Mr. Zaric's apartment by Mr. Tadic and Mr. Simic, what kind of discussions and -- did you have with your neighbours and other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can answer that question. All of those who were not of Serbian ethnicity, this was rather disturbing because the climate throughout that period, about a month prior to the war, was very tense. On a daily basis, Serb families were moving out, not only from the town, I'm talking also about my building. In the evening, only the non-Serb tenants would remain, and I shall explain why. All of them had families and relatives in the neighbouring villages, while the rest of the population remained in their homes. Everybody was preparing for something that we were all feeling, and that was creating tremendous tension in each individual, which includes also me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. Could I now ask you about Cafe AS? Are you familiar with Cafe AS in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I know of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Cafe AS or did you have cause to pass by Cafe AS on a regular basis in March and April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Firstly, in order to get from the town to my home, I had to pass along Cafe AS, so going to town and from town, it was the normal route. The wife of Mr. Tadic had a shop, and I liked shopping. I must say that I personally never was sitting as a patron in that cafe. The cafe has a splendid terrace and all the guests liked sitting on that terrace which is very close to the pavement, the sidewalk, along which I was walking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one clarification of your last answer. You said the wife of Mr. Tadic had a shop and you liked shopping. Do I understand you to mean that Mr. Tadic's wife had a shop which was in the same proximity as the cafe and that you used to frequent the shop and not the cafe?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I liked buying in that shop, and if we look from the direction I was coming, first there was the entrance to that shop, and after that, the entrance to the cafe and the terrace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the time period March and April, 1992, did you ever notice amongst the people who would sit on this terrace you've described, people whom you didn't normally see around Bosanski Samac or did you notice any particular, again, unusual activity in and around the Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: One could observe quite some novelty, quite a novel situation, compared to this very small town we were living in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was, I guess, novel or unique about what you witnessed in Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: One could observe many people who would be sitting. I am speaking of the terrace, not the inside premises of the cafe. It was always full in the morning, afternoon hours, as well as in the evening. So that the turnover of patrons had increased quite a bit. The age structure of these guests was -- they were mainly middle-aged persons. I must admit that also Catholics as well as Muslims were also there, but they were in fewer numbers present, and many, many people of Serb ethnicity, I'm speaking of those people that I know from Samac. The same way we could all -- I would say there were also quite a number of new faces so that I don't know who these people were, but I do know that they were all members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, you just said there were quite a number of new faces, that you didn't know who they were but you did know that they were all members of the 4th Detachment. Why do you conclude they were all members of the 4th Detachment if you did not know who these people were?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm saying this today but I was talking about the events that took place a long time ago, and the events that happened after that time frame prove that these were all members of the 4th Detachment because I recognised them in certain activities and operations that were undertaken later by the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it your testimony that these people who were gathering in Cafe AS were the same people you saw later in military uniform, performing functions on behalf of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, this is before the takeover, did you ever notice whether those people had weapons with them when they were gathering or whether there was any people in military uniform amongst them?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I never saw any personal weapons. By the way, I hate weapons. I also did not notice any uniforms on these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But you saw them later, after the takeover, wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: That's exactly right. Not just in uniforms but also carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, you've mentioned now several times already in your evidence a group called the 4th Detachment. What did you know of the 4th Detachment prior to the takeover of Bosanski Samac on the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, I would go out quite a lot. I mean I would go out every night with my boyfriend to a cafe. And I have to mention here that I'm not a nationalist, I never belonged to any party whatsoever. The same goes for my husband. He was never a nationalist and he never belonged to any party. We were sitting in company with our joint friends and we had the opportunity to discuss not nice things but who of us would be issued weapons and what party they would belong to. The most popular party at that time in our small town -- actually, it's not a party, it was an association, that's what I call it. The most popular one was the 4th Detachment. This was an organisation of people that called themselves the 4th Detachment. They tried in all possible ways to attract as many members as possible. We all knew each other and we also knew who was a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that the 4th Detachment was a military unit that would carry arms?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: At the same time, I knew that a lot of weapons were arriving in Samac. I didn't see this personally, however. I knew that in the villages, weapons were being distributed. Just before the war, in my town, weapons were being distributed to a large extent. I assumed that the weapon was coming from the army, that at least in our area, was mostly Serb. When I'm saying this, I'm referring to the ethnic composition. I personally never saw any weapons before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from where did you obtain the information, then, that there was large distribution of weapons going on, if you personally didn't see it?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I need to emphasise that at that time I lived with my boyfriend, who was very young. He was of military age. And it was very hard for him to avoid all these offers that he was made to get, to receive, to take weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your boyfriend, your then boyfriend, your now husband, did he ever take a weapon or receive a weapon?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No. He never did that, not even during the general mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to go back, you said that there was weapons coming from the army, and that it was mainly going to ethnic Serbs. How did you hear that information?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I got that information from people with which I socialised at that time. We talked about this topic at the Cafe Valentino.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your information came from conversations in the cafe that there was widespread arming of predominantly the Serb population going on; is that a correct understanding of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you now about events on the 16th and 17th of April. Were you at home on the evening of the 16th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Unfortunately, I was not at home. That afternoon, until the late evening, I was out fishing with my boyfriend. Had I been at home, I would have gone to the cafe and I would not be sitting here today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that on the 16th of April, you went fishing. After you finished your fishing expedition, did you then return home to your apartment at number 62, Edvard Kardelja Street?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the evening hours, I went back to my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you and your then boyfriend spend the night in the apartment at 62 Edvard Kardelja Street?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, unfortunately, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some stage during that night, were you awoken by gunfire?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was around 1.30. I didn't take a look at my watch at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell me if you could observe any activity around the streets at this time, at 1.30, or any activity within your apartment block at this time, when you first woke up?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was awoken by my husband, my then boyfriend, who told me, "Jelena, get up. War has started." And I jumped out of bed and I heard shooting. First, he told me to get dressed and that we should wait. You could still hear shooting. And at that time, an ordinary person could get very scared from those sounds. There was a lot of noise in my entranceway at the same time. I found out that that was the beginning of something that we call war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then wait in your apartment block, in your apartment, until you received some information as to what was going on outside?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was dressed and I waited. In the meantime, my neighbours were coming and there was general chaos going on. I would like to emphasise once more that not a single one of us left the entranceway. In the meantime, we heard different kinds of information through the phones. This was a very long and very difficult night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have a telephone in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I did not have a telephone. I used the phone of my neighbour who lived in the apartment above me. His name was Salko Porobic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could you just give me one second?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, if I could, I would just like to introduce to the witness a second diagram, again drawn on her instruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I've left copies with the registrar for the Bench. It's -- the diagram I intend to refer to at the moment has got the ERN in the right-hand corner ending in the four numbers 9072.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, could I ask you to have a look at that diagram that's been placed in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this diagram reflect the occupants of block number 2 of 62 Edvard Kardelja Street?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, just a matter of clarification. Here we see on the screen a diagram with number 070. It was left on the ELMO for a certain reason. And now they are talking about some other diagram that bears number 72. Just to be sure that we are all looking at the same diagram maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, can you just give us the full number of the diagram we are supposed to be looking at?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: 02199072. Counsel for Mr. Zaric is correct. The other one had remained on the ELMO, and the witness now has the diagram ending in 72 in front of her, and I'd ask her to now place it on the ELMO now that she's correctly identified it, for the sake of the defendants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number for it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. This is P68 ID. Thank you. I correct myself: P69 ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, I think from the diagram that's now in front of us, we can see your apartment block on the left-hand side, described as you said earlier, on the second floor of the building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, the third landing, second floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the neighbour who received some phone calls and information as to what was happening was the neighbour living directly above you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: That's exactly right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of information did you receive from your neighbour as to what was going on outside?
