utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The information that we received were extremely bad, very difficult. I found out through my neighbours that there was fighting in the town between the 4th Detachment, the special units, and the people who were trying to save the town. Those were people belonging to the SDA party. I also found out that there were dead, that there were wounded. I found out that the primary school in Samac was on fire. I found out that the first part of town directly to the cemetery was the one worst hit. I know that this was a Muslim part of town. It was also said that there was a slaughter going on. This is -- these information were something that I had never before heard in my entire life. And I was informed that the same thing would also happen in my neighbourhood very soon. Also, we were told that we were not allowed to leave our apartments. We were told that we had to keep our doors open. If the doors were to be locked or closed, then they would shoot at them and the apartments would be entered in that way. We were also told that, when they came, the first contact with this army had to be such that we had to raise our arms and to have our legs mildly spread. The worst thing of all was that we didn't know when all this would happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you Mrs. Kapetanovic. You obviously received a lot of information. I'd like to clarify the sources of that information. The information about the conflict outside, the wounded, the fire at the primary school, did this information come through various telephone calls received by Salko Porobic, or by Salko Porobic and others, or how did you get that information about the conflicts outside and potential fatalities and the fire at the primary school? Was that primarily from Mr. Salko Porobic or from somebody else?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to say that at the entrance 2 of the S62 building, as you can see, there are five floors. At that time, there were families in four floors, and three national -- three ethnic groups who lived in these floors who were there at the time. So information was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, could I just perhaps interrupt you because I think that you're referring now to a diagram, and for the record, it will be much clearer if you just answer the question I asked you first and then we'll go back, using the diagram, and explain what you're now seeking to clarify for the Bench. Okay? So could you please just answer first the information about the conflict and, as I said, potential fatalities and the fire in the primary school? Was that information from, amongst other people, perhaps telephone calls that Salko Porobic received?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The information was coming from different directions, not -- I didn't just get it from Salko Porobic. Everything I mentioned, I found out from my neighbour, Mr. Tubakovic, that had to do with the orders that were given. Those things that I found out about the victims, I found out from the family called Halilovic, and Culumovic as well. So the information was coming from different sources, from more people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mrs. Kapetanovic, now perhaps I could get you to just look at the diagram which has been identified as P69 ID. You've mentioned that some of the information about the victims came from your neighbours Halilovic. That is the Halilovics who lived opposite you on the same floor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was a family of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were a Muslim family. Mrs. Halilovic was from the neighbourhood that I had mentioned before, the first neighbourhood that was hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they told you they'd received a phone call with information about what was going on outside; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned the neighbours by the name of Culumovic; is that correct? They also provided you with some information about victims?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly right. Mr. Culumovic lived -- had a mixed marriage - he's Serb, his wife was Croatian - and he was receiving information from both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned that -- I think you termed it "orders" that you were told, that came from another neighbour by the name of Tubakovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. Mr. Djordje Tubakovic told us how to behave in certain situations that was going to happen to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to clarify for the record, what -- what ethnicity is Mr. Djordje Tubakovic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordje Tubakovic was Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What instructions did he pass on to you as to how you were to behave?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: He told us, I'm repeating, he said that the doors had to be open the, that we had to let them inside, that we had to give them everything they asked for, and that we had to lift our arms and keep our legs slightly widened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when he said that "We had to let them inside and give them everything they asked for," et cetera, who was he referring to by the term "they"?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, we all knew whom we were supposed to let in, because the news that were arriving were saying that members of the 4th Detachment and the special units were coming to liberate the town, and that they were taking over the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned who the 4th Detachment were. The special units, what did you understand the special units to be?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Up until that moment, I had no idea what these special units could be. I just heard that there was a lot of people with Ekavian dialects moving around our town, and we assumed that these were these special people or special units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these Ekavian dialects, do they tend to indicate that someone comes from Serbia proper?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In our small town, we all spoke similarly, with the Ijekavian dialect or the Bosnian dialect, and there were no characteristics present in our language that could be found in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you were waiting at some stage, did these people who you were expecting come to your apartment block, these 4th Detachment and special units?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They finally showed up. We could see them through the windows of my room. I said it was my living-room. It was facing the yard and the entrance of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were any of the defendants accompanying these people who arrived in front of your building?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: At that moment, I didn't know about it, but later, I had the opportunity, one of the defendants standing by my entranceway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which defendant was that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's 13.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning at 0900 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 1.45 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 5th day of June, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
